title: USDA farm payment and loan systems disrupted by a cyber incident; officials say no data lost
date_note: Hackread reports an internal email of 16 November saying a security incident was detected; the page gives no earlier day.
org: US Department of Agriculture (Farm Production and Conservation Business Center)
summary: Hackread reports that a USDA Farm Production and Conservation Business Center email of 16 November said a security incident had been detected and database passwords were being reset. It says Richard Fordyce confirmed on 20 November that it was a cyber threat, not a software update, and that no personally identifiable information was involved and no data was lost. Farm loan, payment and mapping systems were taken offline. Who was behind it and how remain unknown, the article says.
plain: The US Department of Agriculture says a cyber threat, not a software update, disrupted systems that handle farm loans, payments and maps. Officials say no personal data was lost.
exec: Disruption of farm payment and loan systems can delay support to farmers; officials say no personal data was lost.

validation.note: Hackread and a Taiwanese republication of pinnews, which itself cites ABC News and Hackread; the department's own statement was read only as quoted by Hackread.
